gradeScale: Sound and Overall scores on a 1-10 scale with dimensional ratings.

entries.name: Audeze LCD-4
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 7.18/10, overall 6.29/10 (Bass 9.5, Mids 6, Treble 5, X-Factor 10, Comfort 4.5, Value 3.78) (MSRP $4,000).
entries.quote: Monolithic and beautifully-textured bass, reasonable midrange, hit-or-miss treble depending on unit. Extremely heavy, very poor value, but this headphone makes me smile unlike any other.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 480 Pro
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 7.08/10, overall 7.23/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 6.5, Treble 9, X-Factor 7, Comfort 8, Value 6.56) (MSRP $400).
entries.quote: Warm/relaxed tilt overall offset by a slight upper bass scoop results in a coherently balanced signature with smooth treble and a surprisingly spacious presentation. An extremely easy headphone to live with due to its design and comfort.

entries.name: Audio-Technica ATH-W2022
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 7.05/10, overall 6.44/10 (Bass 7.5, Mids 4.5, Treble 8, X-Factor 9.5, Comfort 6, Value 2.76) (MSRP $9,000).
entries.quote: Extremely warm tilted but also still very textured, non-fatiguing but still intense. Hits like a truck. Colored in a way that really works for me and with solid comfort and absolutely gorgeous design

entries.name: Hifiman Edition XV
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 7.03/10, overall 6.66/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 5, Treble 9.5, X-Factor 7, Comfort 5, Value 6.55) (MSRP $400).
entries.quote: Hifiman's best headphone. Coherently warm instead of incoherent warmbright confusion. Rounded, euphonic, potentially a bit dull, but eminently listenable with any music I throw at it.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 650
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.95/10, overall 6.53/10 (Bass 5, Mids 9.5, Treble 6, X-Factor 7, Comfort 5, Value 7.37) (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: Probably the most important audiophile headphone of all time. Decent bass extension for a 30yr old open headphone, reasonably smooth treble, and probably my favorite midrange ever.

entries.name: Aurorus Australis
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.8/10, overall 6.1/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 5.5, Treble 8.5, X-Factor 6.5, Comfort 4, Value 5.52) (MSRP $900).
entries.quote: Lush and profoundly easy to listen to with basically any music. Warmdark enjoyers only; big bass, super warm mids, dark treble. If it were more comfortable I'd probably still own mine, but they're quite heavy.

entries.name: Focal Elex
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.8/10, overall 6.41/10 (Bass 8, Mids 6.5, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 8, Comfort 5, Value 6.24) (MSRP $500).
entries.quote: Warmer/bassier take on the Utopia signature that makes it a little more listenable in exchange for leaving some intensity behind. Hard to say which I prefer, but Elex is way better value.

entries.name: HEDDPhone D1
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.75/10, overall 6.35/10 (Bass 7.5, Mids 9, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 7.5, Comfort 6, Value 5.66) (MSRP $800).
entries.quote: Focal bass + Sennheiser mids + slightly dry treble, but a shockingly well-rounded and complete-sounding offering that is basically the "HD 600 but better bass and tech" that everyone is always asking for.

entries.name: Audeze Maxwell
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.68/10, overall 6/10 (Bass 6, Mids 8, Treble 7, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 4, Value 6.83) (MSRP $300).
entries.quote: Competently tuned across the board and not overly-bright, but potentially too bassy/warm for any sense of excitement or vividness. Too heavy.

entries.name: Focal Utopia
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.58/10, overall 5.83/10 (Bass 8, Mids 5.5, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 8.5, Comfort 4.5, Value 3.56) (MSRP $4,400).
entries.quote: A bit too mid-forward and small-sounding but very punchy and textured. Surprisingly reasonable treble on my head despite claims of it being metallic (think this comes from the mids more than the treble).

entries.name: Aurorus Borealis
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.55/10, overall 5.97/10 (Bass 7, Mids 5, Treble 7.5, X-Factor 7, Comfort 4, Value 5.48) (MSRP $900).
entries.quote: Punches really hard while not battering you with treble. Warm mostly because of how dark it is, otherwise quite cold under 2 kHz. Not neutral, but fun without relying on treble brightness or massive bass.

entries.name: Dan Clark Audio Stealth
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.5/10, overall 5.8/10 (Bass 5, Mids 8, Treble 6.5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 5.5, Value 3.66) (MSRP $4,000).
entries.quote: Very good midrange and the treble is very free of peaks (though has a few dips). A bit too bassy which compounds w/ the treble darkness to result in something that sounds pretty good, but also pretty lifeless.

entries.name: Sony MDR-MV1
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.48/10, overall 6.47/10 (Bass 7, Mids 7.5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 7.5, Comfort 6.5, Value 6.45) (MSRP $400).
entries.quote: Well-rounded V-shape tuning that prioritizes linear bass-to-midrange integration & warmth.. at least until you get to the treble, which may be quite bright. Works very well on my head though. Almost like the AirPods Pro 2 of over-ear headphones.

entries.name: Focal Azurys
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.43/10, overall 5.63/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 7, Treble 6, X-Factor 6, Comfort 3, Value 6.05) (MSRP $550).
entries.quote: Extremely solid tuning across the board with the main downsides being comfort and variability based on clamp force in the treble.

entries.name: Focal Clear
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.38/10, overall 6.06/10 (Bass 7.5, Mids 6, Treble 5, X-Factor 8, Comfort 5, Value 5.59) (MSRP $800).
entries.quote: Sits between Elex and Utopia in terms of listenability and excitement, slightly warmer/smoother than Utopia, slightly less coherent than Elex. Otherwise very similar to Elex, likely within unit variation.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 600
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.35/10, overall 6.09/10 (Bass 5, Mids 8.5, Treble 5, X-Factor 7, Comfort 5, Value 6.77) (MSRP $300).
entries.quote: An excellent evolution from HD 580 Precision that smooths out some (but not all) of the treble issues while losing a bit of intensity/excitement in the process. Legendary for a reason, does very little wrong.

entries.name: HEDDphone 2 GT
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.28/10, overall 5.4/10 (Bass 8, Mids 6.5, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 8.5, Comfort 3, Value 4.34) (MSRP $2,200).
entries.quote: Warm, thick, and rich, with no shortage of texturing or dynamics for bass instruments. Main weakness is rollercoaster treble sharply moving between dips and peaks.

entries.name: Audeze LCD-MX4
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.23/10, overall 5.69/10 (Bass 7.5, Mids 5.5, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 7, Comfort 5, Value 3.96) (MSRP $3,000).
entries.quote: Similar to LCD-4 with a noticeably lesser (but still good) bass presentation andt smoother treble. Lighter and comfier as well.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 550
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.2/10, overall 5.91/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 8.5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 5.5, Value 6.56) (MSRP $350).
entries.quote: Slightly altered typical Sennheiser midrange (less low mid + more 1 kHz makes a meaningful difference), more bass extension, and slightly different treble profile makes for a solid neutral-tilted option. Too expensive though.

entries.name: Audio-Technica ATH-ADX7000
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.18/10, overall 5.56/10 (Bass 7, Mids 6.5, Treble 4, X-Factor 8.5, Comfort 4.5, Value 3.76) (MSRP $3,500).
entries.quote: Warm, full, and smooth in the bass and midrange, with a bit of rollercoastery "flagship" treble that varies based on clamp between "quite good aside from a 10 kHz peak" to "dark"

entries.name: Audeze MM-500
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.15/10, overall 5.24/10 (Bass 6, Mids 7, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 3, Value 4.63) (MSRP $1,700).
entries.quote: Reasonably tuned across the board, but the midrange is a bit too lean and the treble is a bit confused; dark in some spots, bright in others. Overall sounds fine, but not special.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 580 precision
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.13/10, overall 6.06/10 (Bass 5, Mids 8, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 7.5, Comfort 5, Value 7.22) (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: The original reference midrange tuning that started it all. Rougher treble than HD 650 or 600 but with potentially better bass extension depending on which baffle. Black silk > Silver screen > Paper.

entries.name: Capra Audio Satyr 3
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.08/10, overall 6.22/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 6.5, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 6.5, Value 6.61) (MSRP $329).
entries.quote: Well-extended bass, slightly lean midrange, and smooth treble. Solid all-rounder with decent comfort, just feels very rough in the hand due to 3D printed construction.

entries.name: AKG K371
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.08/10, overall 5.58/10 (Bass 6, Mids 7.5, Treble 5, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 3, Value 7.56) (MSRP $150).
entries.quote: Solid bass and great midrange but slightly rough in the mid-treble and very uncomfortable due to the pads being too mushy and the headband providing no padding.

entries.name: ZMF Caldera
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.08/10, overall 5.16/10 (Bass 6, Mids 7, Treble 5, X-Factor 6.5, Comfort 3.5, Value 3.58) (MSRP $4,000).
entries.quote: A unique midrange tuning that balances naturalness, warmth, and clarity quite well, while having some treble coherency issues. Bass is good enough. Very heavy & uncomfortable.

entries.name: Halo Acoustics/Hongshu EH-1 (V2)
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6/10, overall 6.34/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6.5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 8, Comfort 7.5, Value 5.77) (MSRP $650).
entries.quote: Take the very open-feeling acoustic design of the stock config, but add the upper bass/low mdirange it's missing. Still a little bright and sub-bass light, but solid enough to be listenable for most things

entries.name: Audio-Technica ATH-R70x
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.98/10, overall 5.58/10 (Bass 5, Mids 7.5, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 4, Value 6.51) (MSRP $350).
entries.quote: Great midrange with lackluster bass and slightly incoherent treble (dark low-treble, forward mid-treble). Slightly more open alternative to HD 650 with worse comfort.

entries.name: RØDE NTH-100
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.98/10, overall 6.21/10 (Bass 5, Mids 8, Treble 5, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 6.5, Value 7.54) (MSRP $150).
entries.quote: Very warm and dark in the mid-treble, but with a decent overall coherence and a very usable, compact comfort profile.

entries.name: Moondrop Cosmo
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.93/10, overall 5.36/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 5, Treble 7.5, X-Factor 7, Comfort 3, Value 5.23) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: Lean bass, forward center mids, & dark treble makes this sound like a more listenable, less "ethereal" electrostatic headphone. Not super open sounding, but easy to vibe to.

entries.name: Auribus Acoustics Everest
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.88/10, overall 5.32/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 7, Treble 6, X-Factor 4, Comfort 4, Value 5.65) (MSRP $700).
entries.quote: Well-extended bass and solid midrange, slightly over-damped treble repsonse. Main issue is comfort and design, its very heavy and headband weight is not especially well-distributed

entries.name: Denon AH-D2000
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.8/10, overall 5.4/10 (Bass 7, Mids 6.5, Treble 4, X-Factor 6, Comfort 3, Value 7.16) (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: A less V-shaped approach to typical tuning from Foster/Denon closed back headphones. Solid bass texturing, good punch, reasonable midrange, just a bit too bright.

entries.name: Focal Spirit Professional
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.8/10, overall 4.77/10 (Bass 7, Mids 7, Treble 2.5, X-Factor 8, Comfort 0, Value 6.48) (MSRP $350).
entries.quote: The headphone that introduced me to slam and decent tuning; hits dummy hard but quite a rollercoaster in the treble (notably, a big peak around 10 kHz).

entries.name: Shure SRH440
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.78/10, overall 5.4/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6.5, Treble 5, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 2.5, Value 7.99) (MSRP $100).
entries.quote: To this day probably the most competent "consumer" closed back tuning under $150, arguably even better than FiiO FT1 or K371... but some of the worst chassis design/comfort too.

entries.name: Phil Philphone
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.73/10, overall 5.73/10 (Bass 8.5, Mids 4, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 9, Comfort 5, Value 5.38) (MSRP $850).
entries.quote: Arguably one of the most "technical" headphones considering its one of the only ones I know of that has both crazy bass texturing/slam while also being very spacious. Not a neutral headphone at all, but fun.

entries.name: HIFIMAN HE6
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.7/10, overall 4.99/10 (Bass 9, Mids 4.5, Treble 2.5, X-Factor 9, Comfort 2, Value 4.77) (MSRP $1,400).
entries.quote: Hits like a truck at the cost of incredibly harsh, dry treble response and honky unnatural mids. Bottomless bass extension with a ton of texture, but likely too aggressive for some.Terrible comfort.

entries.name: Fiio FT1
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.68/10, overall 5.64/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 6.5, Treble 4, X-Factor 6, Comfort 4.5, Value 7.26) (MSRP $180).
entries.quote: Well-textured and exciting bass presentation, solid midrange tuning, slightly rough/glarey in the treble. Insane value, but definitely a V-shaped headphone

entries.name: ZMF Atrium
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.65/10, overall 4.67/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 7.5, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 2.5, Comfort 3.5, Value 3.61) (MSRP $3,600).
entries.quote: Warm midrange with a slightly muddy bass presentation. Treble is slightly grainy/crashy, while also being a touch too dark in the mid-treble. Confused if it wants to be chill or not, at times.

entries.name: ZMF Aeolus
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.65/10, overall 5.18/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 6, Treble 5, X-Factor 6.5, Comfort 3.5, Value 5.17) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: Decent across the board with a bit of roughness in the lower/mid-treble and a bit of strangeness in the center midrange depending on pads. Too heavy.

entries.name: Fostex TRX00 Mahogany
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.65/10, overall 5.33/10 (Bass 7, Mids 7, Treble 2.5, X-Factor 7, Comfort 4, Value 5.89) (MSRP $550).
entries.quote: Thick, textured bass and a solid midrange tune, but a massive 10 kHz peak and really poor comfort make this competent and fun, but not something I'd ever want to own.

entries.name: Audeze LCD-5
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.63/10, overall 5.23/10 (Bass 6, Mids 4, Treble 7, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 5, Value 3.34) (MSRP $4,500).
entries.quote: A well-extended and smooth-sounding headphone with the right bass/treble tilt, but also a slightly distracting mid-forward coloration.

entries.name: Focal Hadenys
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.63/10, overall 5.28/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 5, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 4, Value 5.69) (MSRP $650).
entries.quote: A bit too mid-bassy, especially when compared to the slightly thinned midrange (too little low-mid, too much 3.5 kHz). Treble is a bit scratchy and over-sharpened. Comfort not great.

entries.name: AKG K361
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.63/10, overall 5.26/10 (Bass 6, Mids 7.5, Treble 4, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 3, Value 7.74) (MSRP $120).
entries.quote: Similar to K371, but with a bit more unevenness in the trouble that results in it sounding a bit grainier and cheaper.

entries.name: Audeze LCD-GX
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.6/10, overall 5.57/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 5.5, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 6, Value 5.29) (MSRP $900).
entries.quote: Similar to Audeze's other Fazor-less designs, solid midrange and dark-leaning treble with full bass extension. Colored, but in a way that at least feels balanced.

entries.name: Focal Utopia 2022
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.53/10, overall 5.1/10 (Bass 5, Mids 5.5, Treble 6, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 5, Value 3.35) (MSRP $4,400).
entries.quote: Utopia but with less bass and treble, which makes it come across incredibly boxy and bereft of anything engaging. A downgrade.

entries.name: Audeze LCD-X (2021)
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.53/10, overall 5.23/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 5.5, Treble 4, X-Factor 7, Comfort 4.5, Value 4.5) (MSRP $1,700).
entries.quote: Arguably Audeze's best midrange tuning, and with solid bass too, but also one of my least favorite treble responses from Audeze; very glassy and bright between 9-12 kHz.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD800s
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.48/10, overall 6.13/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 7.5, Comfort 9, Value 4.72) (MSRP $1,400).
entries.quote: Solid bass extension and a warm midrange tune marred by a lot of mid-treble. Extremely comfortable and well-constructed, and of course very open & spacious sounding.

entries.name: Audeze LCD-2F
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.45/10, overall 5.27/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 6.5, Comfort 4.5, Value 5.13) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: A little bit less refined in mid range and treble than LCD-2 Classic, but the extra upper treble air makes it sound more detailed and alive.

entries.name: HEDD Audio HEDDphone D1
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.45/10, overall 4.72/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 5.5, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 7.5, Comfort 2, Value 4.63) (MSRP $1,500).
entries.quote: Thick bass, slightly honky midrange and a very unique (but still bright) treble response. Interesting presentation of lateral space due to large 6 kHz null. Terrible comfort.

entries.name: Stax SR-X9000
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.4/10, overall 5.34/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 5, Treble 6, X-Factor 6.5, Comfort 6.5, Value 2.9) (MSRP $6,200).
entries.quote: Still a bit bass-shy typical of STAX, but solid mids and treble and my favorite comfort profile from STAX. Has the etheral/open thing going for it but also not entirely bereft of punch.

entries.name: RAAL SR1a
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.33/10, overall 4.84/10 (Bass 1.5, Mids 6, Treble 6.5, X-Factor 8, Comfort 3.5, Value 3.41) (MSRP $4,000).
entries.quote: Very cool presentation of midrange that balances natural warmth with solid articulationlikely due to #nobassbut also solid treble response. Comfort and look is very strange.

entries.name: Halo Acoustics/Hongshu EH-1 (V2)
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.3/10, overall 5.92/10 (Bass 5, Mids 5.5, Treble 4, X-Factor 8, Comfort 7.5, Value 5.61) (MSRP $650).
entries.quote: A soft, lightened presentation paired with a very open-feeling acoustic design, but overall I think this is probably too lean for most people. Pretty comfy for me.

entries.name: Audio-Technica ATH-AD2000X
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.28/10, overall 5.28/10 (Bass 4, Mids 6, Treble 5, X-Factor 6.5, Comfort 5, Value 5.36) (MSRP $800).
entries.quote: Extremely open and airy sounding, without a ton of upper trouble push. Slightly late ear gain results in slight grain, especially due to lack of bass.

entries.name: AKG K553 MKII
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.28/10, overall 5.26/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 6.5, Treble 4, X-Factor 5, Comfort 4, Value 7.39) (MSRP $150).
entries.quote: Predecessor to the K371 with slightly better comfort but higher overall weight and less refinement through the entirety of its response, especially the midrange which was a little cold.

entries.name: Hifiman Susvara
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.25/10, overall 5.24/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 7, Value 2.91) (MSRP $6,000).
entries.quote: Solid bass extension and among Hifiman's best midrange tunings, but a typically bright/gritty Hifiman treble response that makes timbre super artificial. Nice openness.

entries.name: Focal Radiance
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.23/10, overall 5.14/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 5, Treble 4, X-Factor 6, Comfort 5, Value 4.76) (MSRP $1,300).
entries.quote: A fun W-shaped signature that ultimately tilts too far lean and sharp to call it balanced. The more self-damping Stellia driver put in this chassis helps the upper treble relax.

entries.name: Audeze LCD-5
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.2/10, overall 4.71/10 (Bass 4, Mids 5.5, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 4, Value 3.25) (MSRP $4,500).
entries.quote: Potentially the worst flagship successor story; trades LCD-4's exquisitely, thick and textured bass for limp, thin bass, shouty mids, and over-darkened low/mid treble.

entries.name: Koss A/550
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.2/10, overall 5.15/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 6, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 4.5, Value 6.34) (MSRP $350).
entries.quote: A somewhat reasonable midrange tuning marred by excess low treble and slight bass-roll off results in a clacky, crunchy, slightly cheap sounding headphone. Headpad comfort is poor, ear comfort is fine.

entries.name: Hifiman Susvara Unveiled
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.2/10, overall 5.16/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 5.5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 7, Value 2.54) (MSRP $8,000).
entries.quote: Take the original Susvara and add even more low treble grit while reducing the warmth in the midrange. Unilaterally bright instead of warm-bright; worse than the original.

entries.name: RAAL Immanis
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.15/10, overall 4.63/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 5.5, Treble 3, X-Factor 6.5, Comfort 4.5, Value 2.38) (MSRP $9,000).
entries.quote: A mix between something like HE6 and 1266. Colored as hell, overrated as hell, but I see why people enjoy it. Solid bass texturing, interesting space presentation. Terrible treble and industrial design.

entries.name: Aune AC55
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.13/10, overall 4.85/10 (Bass 4, Mids 5.5, Treble 5, X-Factor 6.5, Comfort 2, Value 7.01) (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: Surprisingly punchy and replete bass presentation... but only if you happen to get the seating perfect (on-ears without headbands are cursed). Decent, if slightly honky, midrange and mostly unproblematic treble save for a resonance around 3-4 kHz. Too heavy, poorly designed earclip system.

entries.name: Meze Poet
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.13/10, overall 5.13/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 5.5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 6, Value 4.21) (MSRP $2,000).
entries.quote: Meze's best headphone; the most restrained balance between warmth and clarity they have, with the only downside being a punishing 14 kHz peak. Solid comfort.

entries.name: Shure SRH840
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.13/10, overall 4.9/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 5.5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 2.5, Value 7.36) (MSRP $150).
entries.quote: Uncontroversial V-shape tuning; has extra bass and treble, but in the right spots to actually balance against each other and with a decent midrange profile too. Terrible comfort.

entries.name: Sennheiser HE 1 Orpheus 2
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.08/10, overall 5.03/10 (Bass 5, Mids 5, Treble 5, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 8.5, Value 0) (MSRP $60,000).
entries.quote: Definition of mid. Bass is elevated but textureless due to upper midrange dip, midrange is soupy and dull, treble is both grainy and sibilant. Comfortable as fuck though.

entries.name: Audeze LCD-2 Classic
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.05/10, overall 5.25/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 5, Treble 5, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 6, Value 5.3) (MSRP $800).
entries.quote: Dark midrange and treble but not quite as dark as the Fazor designs in the mids and darkerbut in a good wayin the upper treble than the Fazor-equipped designs.

entries.name: Modhouse Tungsten DS V2
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.05/10, overall 4.81/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 4.5, Value 4.08) (MSRP $2,200).
entries.quote: A slightly (only slightly) warmer take on the Hifiman signature, but ultimately not similar to HE6 at all save for the incredibly stupid drivability (or lack thereof). Heavy but decently comfy.

entries.name: Philphone Closed
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.05/10, overall 5.1/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 5, Treble 4, X-Factor 6.5, Comfort 5, Value 5.03) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: A much chiller take on the Philphone Open's signature, smoothing out the midrange and treble slightly while losing a bit of engagement in the bass. Gets better with clamp but then becomes very uncomfortable, ranked based on impressions with normal/unmodified clamp.

entries.name: E-Mu Teak
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.05/10, overall 4.91/10 (Bass 7, Mids 5.5, Treble 2, X-Factor 7, Comfort 3.5, Value 5.87) (MSRP $500).
entries.quote: Similar to the other Foster biodynas on this list (D2000, TR-x00) but with even worse treble. Slams hard and has good mids, but only realistically an option for people who like a lot of treble.

entries.name: Fostex TH900mk2
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.05/10, overall 4.63/10 (Bass 8.5, Mids 4, Treble 2, X-Factor 7.5, Comfort 3, Value 4.19) (MSRP $2,000).
entries.quote: Super thick and textured bass, but with overly-carved out mids and insanely bright 10-12 kHz region. Uncomfortable, but awesome looking chassis design.

entries.name: Moondrop Edge
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.03/10, overall 5.64/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 4, Treble 6.5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 5.5, Value 8.09) (MSRP $80).
entries.quote: Stock tuning isn't great (especially since ANC nukes bass), shouty, a bit too dark in mid-treble but nice enough upper treble. Real killer is PEQ, after which its great. Lighter/more comfy than most ANC headphones.

entries.name: HEDD Heddphone 2
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.98/10, overall 4.7/10 (Bass 4, Mids 4, Treble 6, X-Factor 6.5, Comfort 3.5, Value 4.17) (MSRP $2,000).
entries.quote: Lacking basically all frequencies except 1 kHz, but surprisingly it kind of works. Textured but chill, very not-dynamic. Comfort is quite poor, though slightly better than GT.

entries.name: Koss Porta Pro
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.95/10, overall 5.47/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 5.5, Treble 6, X-Factor 2.5, Comfort 5.5, Value 8.65) (MSRP $50).
entries.quote: The drippiest headphone of all time, and actually a solid midrange and bass profile for this kind of design. The treble is simply too dark, I'm willing to forgive that for the bass and mids.

entries.name: FiiO JT7
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.95/10, overall 5.51/10 (Bass 6, Mids 4.5, Treble 4, X-Factor 6, Comfort 5.5, Value 7.58) (MSRP $120).
entries.quote: Very similar to the FT1 Pro in the bass and overall presentation, but with a slightly less warm midrange and treble profile, which makes it sound a bit more hardened in its transient attack. Nicely lightweight for a well-extended planar.

entries.name: Dan Clark Audio E3
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.93/10, overall 5.07/10 (Bass 5, Mids 3.5, Treble 6.5, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 6, Value 4.16) (MSRP $2,000).
entries.quote: Bass quite boosted and disjointed relative to midrange which is rather thin, potentially thinnest of any of the AMTS designs. Excellent upper treble but lower treble is papery/dry.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 505
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.93/10, overall 5.28/10 (Bass 3.5, Mids 5.5, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 5.5, Value 6.55) (MSRP $280).
entries.quote: Slightly shouty but smoother overall brother to the HD 560S, with better comfort.

entries.name: FiiO FT1 Pro
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.93/10, overall 5.25/10 (Bass 5, Mids 5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 5, Value 6.84) (MSRP $220).
entries.quote: Hifiman-type signature but trading the upper treble glassiness for lower-treble grain. A fair compromise for those who dislike the upper treble more than low treble, but still rather soft/rough sounding.

entries.name: Hifiman sundara 2020
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.93/10, overall 5.05/10 (Bass 5, Mids 6, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 4.5, Value 6.47) (MSRP $300).
entries.quote: Paradoxically Hifiman's most neutral midrange paired with one of their most confusingly crunchy treble presentations. The 4 kHz region in particular bothers me a lot on this one.

entries.name: Auribus Acoustics Sierra
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.93/10, overall 4.67/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 6.5, Treble 3, X-Factor 3, Comfort 4.5, Value 5.13) (MSRP $900).
entries.quote: Slightly over boosted bass, solid midrange tuning, but terribly harsh treble response. Comfort is very close to being OK, but head padding is insufficient and handfeel is rough.

entries.name: ZMF Auteur
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.88/10, overall 4.4/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 7, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 4, Comfort 3.5, Value 4.5) (MSRP $1,500).
entries.quote: Slight W-shape with a solid midrange tuning but the treble focus and a weirdly rubbery timbre ruin what might've otherwise been a good thing.

entries.name: Stax SR-L300
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.83/10, overall 4.84/10 (Bass 4, Mids 3.5, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 7.5, Comfort 3, Value 5.95) (MSRP $450).
entries.quote: Incredibly open and lightfooted presentation with essentially no bass presence. Less bad in the treble than I would've expected, but midrange is very boxy and strange. Poor comfort.

entries.name: Hifiman He6seV2
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.75/10, overall 4.41/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 3, Treble 6.5, X-Factor 3.5, Comfort 2, Value 6.07) (MSRP $400).
entries.quote: Potentially Hifiman's smoothest treble response, marred by an absolutely cavernous midrange dip that makes it much too warm and soft.

entries.name: Sennheiser hdb 630
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.75/10, overall 5/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 6.5, Treble 2, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 5.5, Value 5.8) (MSRP $500).
entries.quote: Consistent but over-boosted bass with solid low/center-midrange but weird, positioning-sensitive upper midrange (can be shouty, can also be muffled), and really rough 13-14 kHz peak. Surprisingly punchy, not terribly uncomfortable.

entries.name: ZMF Verite
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.73/10, overall 4.4/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 4, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 3.5, Value 3.84) (MSRP $2,500).
entries.quote: Soft and slightly stuffy bass and midrange presentation but with a treble profile that isn't outright disgustingly bright or cloyingly dark. However, still very colored and incoherent.

entries.name: Aurorus Quasar
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.73/10, overall 4.64/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5, Treble 3, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 4.5, Value 4.46) (MSRP $1,500).
entries.quote: Trades Borealis' trademark midrange intensity for a slightly warmer response under 3 kHz but with a LOT more treble (which means it has ruined the Aurorus headphone's best aspect).

entries.name: Dan Clark Audio Noire X
entries.rawName: Dan Clark Audio Noire X Open
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.7/10, overall 4.64/10 (Bass 5, Mids 5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 4, Comfort 4.5, Value 4.95) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: Very similar to the closed back but with a bit more bass control; a bit shouty, a bit incoherent between mid-treble and upper-treble.

entries.name: Moondrop Venus
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.7/10, overall 4.5/10 (Bass 5, Mids 5, Treble 4, X-Factor 5, Comfort 3, Value 5.67) (MSRP $550).
entries.quote: A somewhat better take on the typical Hifiman signature but with too much treble, slightly boxy bass, and a sorely lacking industrial design/comfort scheme.

entries.name: HIFIMAN Arya Unveiled
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.68/10, overall 5.13/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 4.5, Treble 4, X-Factor 5, Comfort 7, Value 4.53) (MSRP $1,400).
entries.quote: Better treble than Hifiman's others, but the bar is in hell. Reasonable midrange profile and bass extension, but nothing really impressive other than the potential for spaciousness.

entries.name: Shure SRH440A
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.63/10, overall 4.81/10 (Bass 5, Mids 4.5, Treble 5, X-Factor 3.5, Comfort 3.5, Value 7.72) (MSRP $100).
entries.quote: SRH440 but with the midrange, bass, and treble all with contrast turned up 200%, which means what was a solid V-shape is now an overblown V-shape that lacks almost all nuance.

entries.name: Koss KPH30i
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.6/10, overall 5.3/10 (Bass 4, Mids 5.5, Treble 5, X-Factor 3, Comfort 5.5, Value 8.83) (MSRP $40).
entries.quote: A solid midpoint between KSC75's overly bright and PortaPro's overly warm signatures, that said I prefer PortaPro's more polite treble response.

entries.name: Moondrop Old Fashioned
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.6/10, overall 5.56/10 (Bass 4, Mids 5, Treble 5, X-Factor 4, Comfort 6, Value 9.4) (MSRP $25).
entries.quote: Basslet, but proportionally dark to balance it, with decent if slightly bark-y sounding midrange. Nothing really special presentation-wise, but arguably a better balance and design/value than KSC75

entries.name: DMS Omega
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.6/10, overall 5.21/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 4.5, Treble 4, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 7.5, Value 4.92) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: Too much mid-bass, an overly-thin midrange, and treble scratchiness that matches the rough feeling of the 3D printed cups.

entries.name: Dan Clark Audio Noire X
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.58/10, overall 4.56/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 4, Comfort 4.5, Value 4.91) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: Competentif a bit overly bassytuning below 2 kHz or so but with a big peak around 2.3 kHz that causes the lower half of the FR to come across thin and shouty. Dark mid-treble, bright upper treble.

entries.name: HarmonicDyne ATHENA
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.55/10, overall 4.91/10 (Bass 3.5, Mids 5, Treble 6, X-Factor 2.5, Comfort 5.5, Value 6.37) (MSRP $300).
entries.quote: Soft, limp bass and competent, if textureless mids, with a surprisingly controlled treble region. Despite it being competent on paper, it feels like listening through coffee filters.

entries.name: Creative Aurvana
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.53/10, overall 5.1/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 4.5, Treble 3, X-Factor 6, Comfort 3, Value 10) (MSRP $15).
entries.quote: A very colored W-shaped headphone but one that's incredibly inexpensive and better than any other headphones you'll find around this price. Not comfortable, not well built, but decent.

entries.name: Neumann NDH30
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.5/10, overall 3.9/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6.5, Treble 2.5, X-Factor 2, Comfort 2, Value 5.51) (MSRP $600).
entries.quote: Competent bass and midrange but with some of the darkest treble I've ever heard. Too dark even for me, who loves dark headphones.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 820
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.48/10, overall 5.14/10 (Bass 3.5, Mids 3.5, Treble 6.5, X-Factor 4, Comfort 8, Value 3.93) (MSRP $2,200).
entries.quote: An overhated headphone because of its absolutely catastrophic measured response under 800 Hz. The bass and midrange are very bad, but the treble is honestly quite good. Comfy.

entries.name: Focal Clear Mg
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.45/10, overall 4.48/10 (Bass 4, Mids 5.5, Treble 4, X-Factor 4, Comfort 5, Value 4.39) (MSRP $1,500).
entries.quote: Imagine Clear but cloyingly dark in the mid-treble and you get this blurry boy. Comes across much too bassy due to treble reduction and midrange honk is also brought forward more.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD660s2
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.4/10, overall 4.73/10 (Bass 3.5, Mids 4.5, Treble 5, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 5, Value 5.71) (MSRP $500).
entries.quote: Boxy and flat like 660S OG but with marginally, barely more treble and bass extension, which realistically only helps make the sense of texturing not outright terrible.

entries.name: HIFIMAN HE1000 Unveiled
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.4/10, overall 4.78/10 (Bass 5, Mids 4, Treble 4, X-Factor 5, Comfort 7, Value 3.18) (MSRP $4,000).
entries.quote: Similar to Arya Unveiled but even brighter and grittier, I cannot really think of a reason to buy this over Arya Unveiled considering it also looks worse.

entries.name: DUNU Arashi
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.4/10, overall 4.65/10 (Bass 5, Mids 6, Treble 2.5, X-Factor 4, Comfort 6, Value 4.65) (MSRP $1,200).
entries.quote: A fairly bog standard take on the Hifiman formula with no real novelty added except for a heavier, yet still fairly comfortable chassis.

entries.name: Audio-Technica ATH-R30x
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.38/10, overall 4.25/10 (Bass 4, Mids 6.5, Treble 3, X-Factor 3.5, Comfort 2, Value 7.66) (MSRP $100).
entries.quote: Kind of like a budget MDR-MV1; V-shaped with excess upper bass and mid-treble, but potentially decent enough for someone who knows they like V-shaped headphones.

entries.name: Focal Celestee
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.38/10, overall 4.8/10 (Bass 7, Mids 2, Treble 3, X-Factor 7.5, Comfort 5, Value 4.86) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: Sucked-out low midrange and boosted 1-2 kHz makes this thing sound more like an IEM than a headphone. Crazy bass punch and texture due to the contrast this creates, though.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 569
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.35/10, overall 4.7/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 3.5, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 3.5, Comfort 4, Value 7.16) (MSRP $150).
entries.quote: What would be a well-damped, competently smooth closed back headphone with poorly managed bass/midrange such that its really only useful to people who want a dark closed back.

entries.name: Beyerdynamic DT 880
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.35/10, overall 4.61/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 4.5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 3.5, Comfort 4, Value 6.93) (MSRP $180).
entries.quote: Weirdly reminiscent of HD 800S mids where everything feels distant, cloudy and slightly muffled, but its treble presentation leans more towards mid-treble brightness. Fine for bright enjoyers, I guess.

entries.name: Focal Stellia
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.35/10, overall 4.48/10 (Bass 6, Mids 3, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 5, Value 3.52) (MSRP $3,000).
entries.quote: Kind of like Celestee if it had more midrange and treble control but also less bass slam. Nothing really special outside some decent bass texturing.

entries.name: Meze Elite
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.3/10, overall 4.45/10 (Bass 4, Mids 4.5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 4, Comfort 6, Value 3.16) (MSRP $4,000).
entries.quote: My favorite headphone in the Empyrean chassis due to the well-controlled 10 kHz area and the slight tilt towards clarity elsewhere vs. OG Empyrean.

entries.name: Dan Clark Audio Aeon 2 Noire
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.3/10, overall 4.42/10 (Bass 4, Mids 4.5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 4, Comfort 4.5, Value 4.97) (MSRP $900).
entries.quote: Surprisingly boxy midrange with a lumpy upper-bass hump and typical planar treble. Not exceedingly good at anything, but not terrible either.

entries.name: Dan Clark Audio EXPANSE
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.25/10, overall 4.47/10 (Bass 3.5, Mids 5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 3.5, Comfort 6.5, Value 3.14) (MSRP $4,000).
entries.quote: Weirdly, didn't sound as bassy as I expected. Similar mids to E3 where the low mid is too scooped and the lower treble transition is pushed so it sounds dry. Upper treble not as smooth.

entries.name: Sony MDR-Z1R
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.15/10, overall 4.73/10 (Bass 7, Mids 2.5, Treble 2.5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 6.5, Value 4.01) (MSRP $1,900).
entries.quote: Dense, heavy bass response marred by shouty midrange and incredibly piercing treble. Comfortable and cool looking, but hard to recommend.

entries.name: Koss KSC75
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.1/10, overall 5.06/10 (Bass 3.5, Mids 5, Treble 4, X-Factor 3.5, Comfort 5.5, Value 9.04) (MSRP $30).
entries.quote: The budget GOAT, especially when put on a Parts Express headband that smooths the treble and raises the bass a bit. That said, still too bright and shouty for me.

entries.name: HIFIMAN Ananda
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.08/10, overall 4.83/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 4.5, Treble 2, X-Factor 5, Comfort 6.5, Value 5.89) (MSRP $400).
entries.quote: Very similar to the other egg-shaped Hifiman headphones but with particularly shrill upper treble with a weirdly hazy presentation to the midrange.

entries.name: Shure SRH840A
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.05/10, overall 4.39/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 3.5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 3.5, Comfort 3.5, Value 7.07) (MSRP $150).
entries.quote: Takes the V-shape that worked in the SRH840 and makes it unhinged. Still has elevations in the right place, they're just way too big now along with a sucked out midrange.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD490 Pro
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.05/10, overall 5.07/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 3.5, Treble 4, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 7.5, Value 5.94) (MSRP $380).
entries.quote: HD 800's mids and HD 560S's treble but with extra bass extension (Producer Pads) or weirdly 1kHz forward mids and strange upper midrange/low treble transition (Mixing Pads)

entries.name: ETA Mini Open
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.05/10, overall 3.68/10 (Bass 3, Mids 6, Treble 3, X-Factor 4, Comfort 1, Value 6.23) (MSRP $300).
entries.quote: Potentially the least comfortable headphone I've ever worn (on-ear design with metal grilles), reasonable mids overly darkened/muffled overall response.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 660 S
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.03/10, overall 4.4/10 (Bass 3.5, Mids 4.5, Treble 5, X-Factor 2, Comfort 5, Value 6.03) (MSRP $350).
entries.quote: Weirdly sucked out presence region and sorely lacking bass extension recenter the signature around 1kHz which makes for a surprisingly boxy, flat listen.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 599
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.03/10, overall 4.32/10 (Bass 3.5, Mids 4.5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 3, Comfort 4, Value 6.49) (MSRP $240).
entries.quote: Sennheiser's most V-shaped headphone in the 5 series, with very crunchy treble and a sucked out upper midrange that makes the bass sound messy and one-note.

entries.name: Beyerdynamic DT1990 Pro
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4/10, overall 4.17/10 (Bass 4, Mids 5.5, Treble 3, X-Factor 3, Comfort 4, Value 5.99) (MSRP $360).
entries.quote: Somehow even less punchy than the 880 and 990 despite better bass-extension. Solid mids but typical of Beyer the mid-treble is truly heinous.

entries.name: Apple AirPods Max
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4/10, overall 4.02/10 (Bass 7, Mids 4, Treble 2, X-Factor 3, Comfort 3.5, Value 5.48) (MSRP $550).
entries.quote: Awesome, consistent bass presentation and boost placement, marred by overly-muffled mids and some of the worst treble I've ever experienced in the 8-12 kHz region. Too heavy with weird ergonomics/headband.

entries.name: Sony MDR-F1
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.95/10, overall 5.53/10 (Bass 0.5, Mids 4, Treble 6, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 9.5, Value 6.2) (MSRP $300).
entries.quote: No bass at all, but a somewhat okay midrange and honestly guilty-pleasure-level dark treble response. Completely lifeless and devoid of treble texture, but enjoyable and super comfy.

entries.name: Audeze LCD-1
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.95/10, overall 4.08/10 (Bass 3.5, Mids 4.5, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 3, Value 6.01) (MSRP $350).
entries.quote: A portable planar that sounds like if Audeze was making a Hifiman but forgot to add any low-midrange or bass presence. Very thin but also quite open feeling. Poor headband comfort.

entries.name: Philips Fidelio X2HR
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.95/10, overall 4.9/10 (Bass 5, Mids 5, Treble 2, X-Factor 4, Comfort 7, Value 6.69) (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: One of the grainiest, saddest treble responses I'm aware of in headphones. Which is such a shame because the bass and midrange are actually quite competent.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 580
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.9/10, overall 4.13/10 (Bass 3, Mids 6, Treble 2, X-Factor 5, Comfort 4, Value 5.56) (MSRP $500).
entries.quote: Essentially an HD 600 with a black-paper baffle, which is to say its a brighter/more bass-light HD 600. Not my jam.

entries.name: Meze 105 Aer
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.88/10, overall 4.17/10 (Bass 5, Mids 4.5, Treble 3, X-Factor 2.5, Comfort 4.5, Value 5.83) (MSRP $400).
entries.quote: Incredibly scratchy and harsh low treble with overblown bass and a hole in the mid treble. Sounds like an HD 599 with pocket lint shoved in the earcups.

entries.name: Meze Empyrean
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.85/10, overall 4.18/10 (Bass 4, Mids 4.5, Treble 3, X-Factor 4, Comfort 6, Value 3.37) (MSRP $3,000).
entries.quote: Soupy, incredibly bloated, and shrill as hell in the upper treble. Never really saw the appeal of this one despite its technically "okay" midrange, even though I prefer it to Empyrean II.

entries.name: Audeze CRBN
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.83/10, overall 4.26/10 (Bass 3, Mids 4, Treble 4, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 6.5, Value 2.87) (MSRP $4,500).
entries.quote: Typical estat thinness, but made even more dramatic due to the presence of added 3 kHz energy. Quite comfortable, but very dry sounding and limp.

entries.name: Audeze MM-100
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.83/10, overall 3.6/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 4, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 3, Comfort 1.5, Value 5.81) (MSRP $400).
entries.quote: Somehow slight changes from the MM 500 formula make for a massively worse headphone. Glarey, thin, shouty, and even more coherent between mid and upper treble. Also way less comfortable.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 540 Gold
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.83/10, overall 4.41/10 (Bass 3, Mids 5, Treble 3, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 5.5, Value 5.54) (MSRP $500).
entries.quote: An interesting take on an HD800-like signature but with different chassis acoustics and a markedly more "thin" presentation because of it. I could see how this would appeal to estat enjoyers.

entries.name: Meze Liric II
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.83/10, overall 4.1/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 5, Treble 2, X-Factor 4, Comfort 5.5, Value 3.86) (MSRP $2,000).
entries.quote: They fixed the midrangehonestly, its competentbut the bass now has no texture and the upper treble is ridiculously boosted

entries.name: Audio-Technica ATH-M40x
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.8/10, overall 3.9/10 (Bass 3.5, Mids 3.5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 3.5, Comfort 1.5, Value 7.48) (MSRP $100).
entries.quote: A bit over boosted in the bass, a bit thin in the mid range, and a bit rough in the treble, with a pretty uncomfortable chassis too. Not completely irredeemable, but certainly not good.

entries.name: Warwick Acoustics Bravura
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.78/10, overall 3.07/10 (Bass 4, Mids 3.5, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 1, Value 2.45) (MSRP $6,300).
entries.quote: Potentially the most intrusively bad acoustic design I've encountered, makes my head feel like its in a fishbowl. Unoriginal W-shape "flagship" tuning, slightly better than Aperio but still not good.

entries.name: Meze 109 Pro
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.73/10, overall 4.04/10 (Bass 5, Mids 3.5, Treble 3, X-Factor 3.5, Comfort 4.5, Value 4.94) (MSRP $800).
entries.quote: Similarly harsh but with more shimmer than 105 AER, still too much bass and a scooped midrange. Sounds like HD 599 but made even more V-shaped.

entries.name: Meze Liric
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.68/10, overall 4.27/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 2.5, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 6, Value 3.81) (MSRP $2,000).
entries.quote: Sounds like an IEM with weeb-like forward 1-2 kHz, a poorly placed bass shelf, and no real sense of treble control.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 560S
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.58/10, overall 3.71/10 (Bass 3.5, Mids 5, Treble 2.5, X-Factor 3, Comfort 2.5, Value 6.57) (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: Thin, dry, scratchy, grainy, basically all of the bad parts of 5-series treble but with a super-thin midrange and no bass tactility despite decent extension. Too clampy.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD620s
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.55/10, overall 4.23/10 (Bass 4, Mids 4, Treble 3, X-Factor 3, Comfort 5.5, Value 5.88) (MSRP $350).
entries.quote: A rollercoaster with badly-managed bass, boxy midrange, and rollercoaster-tier treble littered with narrow band resonances. Underdamped. Comfy.

entries.name: ZMF Caldera Closed
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.53/10, overall 3.43/10 (Bass 3, Mids 4, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 3.5, Comfort 3.5, Value 3) (MSRP $3,700).
entries.quote: An absolute rollercoaster from beginning to end, W-shaped as hell. Overdone bass boost, then low mid cut, then center/upper mid push, then a massive clarity cut. Colored as hell in a way I do not enjoy.

entries.name: HIFIMAN EDITION XS
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.5/10, overall 3.74/10 (Bass 5, Mids 3.5, Treble 1.5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 2.5, Value 6.13) (MSRP $280).
entries.quote: One of Hifiman's bassiest/warmest egg-shaped designs under 2 kHz but also potentially the brightest above 10 kHz. Super plasticky and sharp sounding. Bad comfort.

entries.name: Abyss 1266 Phi TC
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.48/10, overall 2.99/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 2, Treble 2, X-Factor 6, Comfort 1, Value 2.41) (MSRP $6,000).
entries.quote: Excessively W-shaped response with its only potential benefit being an unruly subbass peak, dependent on positioning. Terrible industrial design and comfort.

entries.name: Beyerdynamic DT 990 (600 Ohm)
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.38/10, overall 3.73/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 6, Treble 1, X-Factor 1, Comfort 4, Value 6.7) (MSRP $170).
entries.quote: Not atrociously bad midrange or bass performance for an open-back headphone, but some of the worst treble I've ever heard in an over-ear headphone. Insanely bright.

entries.name: Beyerdynamic DT 700 Pro X
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.35/10, overall 4.17/10 (Bass 3.5, Mids 3, Treble 4, X-Factor 2.5, Comfort 5.5, Value 6.12) (MSRP $270).
entries.quote: Similar to DT770 with marginally less painful treble, but surprisingly not as comfortable as I'd have thought given the thick pads. Thin mids, overcooked bass, just not very good.

entries.name: Austrian Audio Hi-X60
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.33/10, overall 4.52/10 (Bass 4, Mids 3, Treble 3, X-Factor 3.5, Comfort 7.5, Value 5.64) (MSRP $400).
entries.quote: Takes the Hi-X55's design and changes some of the damping to somewhat curtail the biggest issues in the bass and midrange. Treble still kind of sucks, comfort still excellent.

entries.name: Philips SHP9500
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.3/10, overall 4.4/10 (Bass 3, Mids 4, Treble 3, X-Factor 3, Comfort 6, Value 7.31) (MSRP $100).
entries.quote: Feels like a mouth full of sand. Grainy, dry, and tasteless.

entries.name: Warwick Acoustics Aperio
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.28/10, overall 2.43/10 (Bass 3.5, Mids 3, Treble 2.5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 1, Value 0) (MSRP $40,000).
entries.quote: Potentially the most intrusively bad acoustic design I've encountered, makes my head feel like its in a fishbowl. Unoriginal W-shape "flagship" tuning meant to do everything but convey good timbre.

entries.name: Abyss Diana TC
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.2/10, overall 3.1/10 (Bass 5, Mids 2, Treble 2, X-Factor 5, Comfort 2.5, Value 2.65) (MSRP $4,500).
entries.quote: Like the 1266, W-shaped to a fault, but without the fun bass party trick. Slightly better, but still terrible comfort and industrial design.

entries.name: Final D8000 Pro
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.18/10, overall 3.65/10 (Bass 4, Mids 2.5, Treble 2.5, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 5.5, Value 2.65) (MSRP $4,500).
entries.quote: Typical W-shaped planar but with a less bass tactility than these kinds of signatures typically have, likely down to the downright excessive treble.

entries.name: Moondrop Horizon
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.18/10, overall 3.64/10 (Bass 2.5, Mids 6, Treble 1.5, X-Factor 2, Comfort 4, Value 6.43) (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: Super dark and noticeably bass-rolled, this headphone makes PortaPro sound incredibly detailed and high-res. Comfort would be great if the headband clamped more.

entries.name: Audio-Technica ATH-ADX5000
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.15/10, overall 3.2/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 2.5, Treble 2.5, X-Factor 3.5, Comfort 3, Value 3.5) (MSRP $2,200).
entries.quote: W-shaped response with grainy, sizzling treble and wonky mid range timbre. Also incredibly uncomfortable due to lack of headband padding

entries.name: HIFIMAN Arya Organic
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.15/10, overall 4.2/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 3, Treble 1.5, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 7, Value 4.64) (MSRP $860).
entries.quote: Somehow brighter than Arya Stealth but also less grating because most of it is relegated to upper treble, but still too thin due to overly reduced upper bass/low midrange.

entries.name: Focal Bathys
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.08/10, overall 3.18/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 2.5, Treble 3, X-Factor 2, Comfort 2.5, Value 4.87) (MSRP $700).
entries.quote: Loose, lumpy bass with a muddy midrange and metallic, shrieky treble. Terrible headband comfort.

entries.name: Focal Elegia
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.08/10, overall 3.59/10 (Bass 3, Mids 4, Treble 2.5, X-Factor 2.5, Comfort 5, Value 4.43) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: Weirdly cuppy but also shouty mids, rolled off bass, and super rocky treble littered with narrow band resonances. Comfort is decent.

entries.name: Abyss Diana MR
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.08/10, overall 3.09/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 2, Treble 2, X-Factor 5, Comfort 2.5, Value 3.1) (MSRP $3,000).
entries.quote: Like the 1266, W-shaped to a fault, but without the fun bass party trick. Slightly better, but still terrible comfort and industrial design.

entries.name: Sony MDR-7506
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.05/10, overall 3.38/10 (Bass 2, Mids 3, Treble 4, X-Factor 3, Comfort 1.5, Value 7.22) (MSRP $100).
entries.quote: Unilaterally bright but in a way that might make sense for someone who likes raw Diffuse Field... I don't though, so its just shouty and gigabright for me. Terrible earpad comfort

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 58X
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.98/10, overall 3.72/10 (Bass 3.5, Mids 4.5, Treble 1, X-Factor 3, Comfort 4.5, Value 6.47) (MSRP $180).
entries.quote: Imagine HD 660S2 but with considerably rougher low treble and a less open/premium feeling chassis.

entries.name: BeyerDynamic DT770
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.95/10, overall 3.64/10 (Bass 2.5, Mids 4, Treble 2.5, X-Factor 2.5, Comfort 4, Value 6.61) (MSRP $160).
entries.quote: Simultaneously boomy and recessed bass, cloyingly, translucently-thin midrange, and extremely bright treble. Looks more comfortable than it is.

entries.name: Hifiman Arya Stealth
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.95/10, overall 3.92/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 4, Treble 0.5, X-Factor 1.5, Comfort 7, Value 5.11) (MSRP $550).
entries.quote: Probably the single most painful treble response I've ever encountered in an over-ear headphone. Bass is actually okay, mids aren't great, but the treble... jesus christ.

entries.name: Fostex T50RP Mk3
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.93/10, overall 3.25/10 (Bass 3, Mids 4.5, Treble 1.5, X-Factor 2.5, Comfort 2.5, Value 6.33) (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: Crazy sibilant and sharp treble with wonky mids and a limp bass profile. Non-existent earpad depth and lack of headband padding also mean its uncomfortable as hell.

entries.name: Austrian Audio Composer
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.9/10, overall 3.62/10 (Bass 5, Mids 3, Treble 1, X-Factor 3, Comfort 6.5, Value 3.15) (MSRP $2,700).
entries.quote: Massive upper midrange suckout means what would otherwise be solid, linearly extended bass ends up textureless and indistinct. Absolutely terrible, crashy sounding treble response, boosted across the board. Nice design, though.

entries.name: Meze Empyrean II
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.85/10, overall 3.53/10 (Bass 3, Mids 3.5, Treble 1.5, X-Factor 4, Comfort 6, Value 3) (MSRP $3,000).
entries.quote: Extremely sharp and gritty low treble with weirdly cuppy, sucked out upper mids and bloated bass. I have no idea how the hell its worse than the original, but they managed it.

entries.name: Audio-Technica ATH-M50x
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.63/10, overall 2.88/10 (Bass 3, Mids 3.5, Treble 2, X-Factor 1.5, Comfort 1.5, Value 6.54) (MSRP $150).
entries.quote: Even more incoherence of bass and midrange with one of the harshest low-treble responses I'm familiar with. Terrible comfort profile.

entries.name: Hifiman HE400SE
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.58/10, overall 3.06/10 (Bass 4, Mids 2, Treble 2.5, X-Factor 1.5, Comfort 2, Value 6.9) (MSRP $110).
entries.quote: Midrange that sounds like things are down a long hallway filled with packing foam and sizzly, sibilant treble. Bass extension very decent for a cheap open back headphone.

entries.name: Dan Clark Audio Ether CX
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.5/10, overall 3.33/10 (Bass 2.5, Mids 2, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 1.5, Comfort 5.5, Value 4.18) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: Sounds like an LCD-2c with a metric ton of damping; limp bass, lifeless mids, and perhaps the most dead treble i've heard.

entries.name: Audeze LCD-2
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.43/10, overall 3.34/10 (Bass 2.5, Mids 1.5, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 2, Comfort 5.5, Value 4.27) (MSRP $900).
entries.quote: Shouty and dark, unnecessarily heavy, though strangely not as offensively bright in the upper treble as the LCD-XC

entries.name: Audeze LCD-XC
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.43/10, overall 2.77/10 (Bass 2.5, Mids 1.5, Treble 1.5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 2, Value 3.83) (MSRP $1,300).
entries.quote: One of the thinnest headphones I've heard, practically no bass presence and a very shouty midrange. Also heavy as hell.

entries.name: AKG K240 Studio
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.3/10, overall 3.35/10 (Bass 2, Mids 3, Treble 2, X-Factor 2, Comfort 4, Value 7.31) (MSRP $70).
entries.quote: Thin, limp, muffed in the mids but sharp in the treble with no palpabale bass weight. Extremely lightweight but the leatherette used for pads/headband is incredibly cheap/plasticky.

entries.name: Grell OAE1
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.25/10, overall 2.75/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 2.5, Treble 0, X-Factor 2.5, Comfort 2.5, Value 5.51) (MSRP $300).
entries.quote: Decent bass extension for an open headphone with harsh mids due to excessive 3-5 kHz and outright wrong treble. Also a terribly clampy headphone with bad headband comfort.

entries.name: ZMF Atrium Closed
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.03/10, overall 2.36/10 (Bass 3, Mids 2.5, Treble 1, X-Factor 1.5, Comfort 3.5, Value 2.76) (MSRP $2,600).
entries.quote: V-shaped as hell with sucked out upper mids and some of the shrillest treble I've heard, wild that its from a ZMF headphone (they usually trend dark).

entries.name: Grado SR60x
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 1.85/10, overall 2.59/10 (Bass 2, Mids 2, Treble 1.5, X-Factor 2, Comfort 2, Value 6.61) (MSRP $100).
entries.quote: Shouty, bright, basslet, uncomfortable, I really see no reason for this headphone to exist when the Koss options have a much better presentation and comfort profile.

entries.name: AKG K52
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 1.6/10, overall 4.06/10 (Bass 1, Mids 1, Treble 2.5, X-Factor 2, Comfort 8.5, Value 8.39) (MSRP $20).
entries.quote: Terrible basically across the board except for marginally non-fatiguing treble. Incredibly comfortable due to weighing almost nothing, having suspension strap, and having massive earpads.

entries.name: HiFiMAN HE-R10 Dynamic Version
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 1.55/10, overall 2.22/10 (Bass 2, Mids 0.5, Treble 2.5, X-Factor 1, Comfort 3.5, Value 3.28) (MSRP $1,300).
entries.quote: Muddy, slightly grainy, cavernously hollow. No reason for this headphone to exist.

entries.name: Yamaha YH-5000SE
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 1.03/10, overall 2.4/10 (Bass 2, Mids 1, Treble 0.5, X-Factor 0.5, Comfort 8, Value 1.17) (MSRP $5,000).
entries.quote: Looks cool, but has simultaneously muffled and shouty midrange, sloppy bass, and ringy splashy treble.

entries.name: Austrian Audio Hi-X55
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 1/10, overall 2.8/10 (Bass 1, Mids 1, Treble 1, X-Factor 1, Comfort 7.5, Value 4.34) (MSRP $350).
entries.quote: If Audivina didn't exist, this would be the worst closed back headphone I'm aware of. Gets literally nothing right, massive resonances in bass and midrange and stupidly bright treble. Great comfort though.

entries.name: Harmonicdyne x Zeos Eris
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 1/10, overall 2.53/10 (Bass 1, Mids 1, Treble 1, X-Factor 1, Comfort 6, Value 4.53) (MSRP $300).
entries.quote: Terrible across the board, bordering on broken, saved only by its decent comfort profile.

entries.name: HIFIMAN Audivina
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 0.5/10, overall 1.03/10 (Bass 0.5, Mids 0.5, Treble 0.5, X-Factor 0.5, Comfort 2.5, Value 1.38) (MSRP $2,000).
entries.quote: Simply put, one of the worst audiophile headphones on the planet. Bass recessed and poorly extended, midrange wonky as hell, and ear-splitting treble. Terrible acoustics, too.

entries.name: Prisma Lumen
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 8.53/10, overall 8/10 (MSRP 1300).
entries.quote: Hard-hitting, slightly forward bass, faultless midrange, and the smoothest treble response I've ever heard in an IEM. Excellent comfort profile and Apple-level industrial design/look. Truly neutral.

entries.name: CrinEar Reference
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 7.95/10, overall 7.51/10 (MSRP 350).
entries.quote: A nimble take on neutral that prioritizes timbre and texture in roughly equal measure. Slightly tilted towards clarity vs. absolute accuracy, but still very competent.

entries.name: Noble Onyx
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 7.48/10, overall 6.97/10 (MSRP 3200).
entries.quote: An enveloping, chesty bass presentation with a warm, cozy midrange and a silken, but controlled treble rseponse. Super fun, without treble peaks, with a massive imaging trick. Unvented/big shell with a great nozzle profile, so not uncomfortable but not long-term comfy either.

entries.name: TruthEar Pure
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 7.4/10, overall 6.82/10 (MSRP 90).
entries.quote: I helped tune it, so I'm biased... but its definitely not perfect. Not too much sub-bass or treble, warm + forgiving midrange, but if I had my way it would have a bit less bloom, more relaxed mid-treble (length mode), and better shell comfort.

entries.name: Softears Volume S
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 7.23/10, overall 7.28/10 (MSRP 320).
entries.quote: Exemplary bass and treble balance, only weakness is a bit too much bias towards upper midrange/lower treble, so timbre isn't perfect. Slams hard, great texturing for bass instruments in particular. Best with narrow bore tips.

entries.name: CrinEar Nightfall
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 7/10, overall 7.13/10 (MSRP 100).
entries.quote: Great bass and midrange balance marred by a "harmonically simple" treble response solely punctuated by two length-based peaks (and almost nothing else). Great comfort profile & accessories for a budget IEM and likely the best starting point for most new enthusiasts.

entries.name: Apple AirPods Pro 2
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.98/10, overall 7.68/10 (MSRP 200).
entries.quote: Unreasonably well tuned for a mass-market consumer product. Reasonably dynamic and thick bass, solid if slightly blurry midrange, and a bit of extra mid-treble. My most comfortable IEM.

entries.name: Shuoer Cadenza 12
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.98/10, overall 6.04/10 (MSRP 2300).
entries.quote: Truly convincing note weight and density, excellent dynamic expressiveness, texturing, & dynamics of instrument size. Midrange is also very coherent & natural sounding. Downside is awful treble brightness and large shell.

entries.name: Status Pro X GoldenSound Edition
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.9/10, overall 6.6/10 (MSRP 280).
entries.quote: Bouncy mid-bass adequately balanced by slightly texture-forward mids, treble mostly sensible & controlled, while punctuated by slight 6.8 / 12 kHz emphases. Solid consumer tuning that abandons neither balance nor "fun"

entries.name: Moondrop Space Travel 2
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.6/10, overall 6.2/10 (MSRP 30).
entries.quote: Similar to Volume S but wireless with less impressive bass. Upper midrange isn't quite smooth enough, a bit of glare around 3.1 kHz. Insane value, if it didn't have bad comfort & battery depletion to worry about it would be the go-to budget IEM.

entries.name: Nightjar Singularity
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.55/10, overall 6/10 (MSRP 1300).
entries.quote: Tons of bass, but actually well-placed in terms of corner frequency and deftly balanced/integrated with its midrange. Not neutral, but intentional. A treble compromise that actually makes sense for a single DD.

entries.name: SUBTONIC STORM
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.55/10, overall 5.46/10 (MSRP 6000).
entries.quote: Fantastic midrange and solid bass, treble is just too much for me. Still manages to punch very hard and express timbre mostly competently despite excess energy in uppermost octaves. Very large unvented shell means comfort is poor.

entries.name: ZIIGAAT LUSH
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.5/10, overall 6.23/10 (MSRP 180).
entries.quote: Unique execution of a warm, neutral-ish signature. Bit too much bass, a bit too relaxed in ear gain, and a bit too much low treble, but overall very reasonable, if a bit stodgy. Comfort is meh, not well-molded enough.

entries.name: Softears RSV mk2
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.4/10, overall 5.99/10 (MSRP 700).
entries.quote: Mid-bass focused with solid midrange tuning but a lot of upper treble, however treble that can actually be addressed quite well with tip-rolling; narrow for less air, wide for more air. Still incoherence between bass largesse and slight thinness of midrange/treble, but quite respectable and does very little wrong. Huge shell, but also a weirdly comfortable one.

entries.name: 64 Audio Nio
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.38/10, overall 6.49/10 (MSRP 1700).
entries.quote: Fun, punchy bass presentation partially due to colored mids and low treble, and the least annoying upper treble I've heard from 64 Audio.

entries.name: Prisma Lux
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.33/10, overall 6.34/10 (MSRP 1300).
entries.quote: Fantastic midrange. Bass is a bit bulbous and lacks a bit of texture due to overwhelming the midrange. Lower treble control is excellent but upper treble is much too forward; sounds very glassy, but I think for V-shaped sets this is among the most put-together and intentional feeling ones next to Storm and U6t.

entries.name: 64 Audio U6t
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.28/10, overall 6.29/10 (MSRP 1300).
entries.quote: Extremely competent bass and midrange tuning but with excessively splashy and metallic upper treble, with a slight bit of grittiness somewhere in the low treble as well. Not smooth, but has enough special sauce that the compromise may be worth it to some.

entries.name: 64 Audio Tia Trio
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.2/10, overall 6.32/10 (MSRP 2300).
entries.quote: Surprisingly solid midrange timbre despite looking weird when measured, reasonably engaging and textured bass, and less problematic upper treble than expected. Comfort gets half-point reduction for lack of venting.

entries.name: Kinera URD
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.15/10, overall 5.46/10 (MSRP 650).
entries.quote: Shockingly well rounded, solid bass tuning and texturing, midrange akin to 64 Audio's lesser models but with better bass vitality and treble control. Huge shell with strange pressurisation feeling.

entries.name: CRINEAR DAYBREAK
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.1/10, overall 6.21/10 (MSRP 170).
entries.quote: Fantastic midrange, with moderate excess of bass and treble. Needs wide bore tips to rebalance the treble region but otherwise its a competently tuned set and a fantastic value.

entries.name: Hisenior Mega 5 EST
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.1/10, overall 5.96/10 (MSRP 550).
entries.quote: Great midrange, smooth and relaxed low/mid treble, moderate bass and upper treble excess. Slightly blurred and distant presentation, but also uniquely relaxing despite extra shimmer.

entries.name: Final E500
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 6.05/10, overall 6.69/10 (MSRP 25).
entries.quote: QC on these are terrible, but if it wasn't, these would be OP. Bass rolloff, but extremely well tuned (if warm) midrange and a mostly relaxed treble response But again, DO NOT BUY. Only pain will befall you.

entries.name: Sony IER-M7
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.98/10, overall 6.5/10 (MSRP 500).
entries.quote: Great midrange tuning, middling bass performance, mostly polite treble that only works with stock narrow bore tips. Incredibly comfortable shell design, but docked one point for lack of venting.

entries.name: Vision Ears PHöNIX
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.98/10, overall 5.4/10 (MSRP 4200).
entries.quote: Fun bass presentation and a surprisingly not-terrible midrange. Bit of hash in the lower and upper treble. Interesting spaciousness presentation.

entries.name: ZIIGAAT ODYSSEY
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.95/10, overall 5.75/10 (MSRP 230).
entries.quote: Lovely, if soft and slightly feathered midrange tuning, with a reasonable treble profile, marred by a bass-prioritized signature that ends up sounding quite plodding. Solid timbre overall though.

entries.name: Apple AirPods Pro 3
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.88/10, overall 5.93/10 (MSRP 250).
entries.quote: Pretty much a standard consumer V-shape. Scratchy, plasticky treble and overblown mid-bass are obtrusive enough to make this less good than the APP2, which is a shame because the midrange and ANC/transparency are exceptional.

entries.name: Symphonium x Nightjar Meteor
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.75/10, overall 6.06/10 (MSRP 600).
entries.quote: Noticeably overcooked in the bass and uppermost treble, but a lush/romantic midrange and a relaxed take on lower treble makes this one of my favorite "ultra-colored" IEMs.

entries.name: DUNU Mirai
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.75/10, overall 5.21/10 (MSRP 950).
entries.quote: Similar to 64 Audio U4s, with leaner mids but better bass. Still too sibilant in the treble, but overall it's significantly more impactful and visceral than most of 64 Audio's other IEMs.

entries.name: Kiwi Ears KE4
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.7/10, overall 6.06/10 (MSRP 200).
entries.quote: Excellent midrange, excessive bass and incredibly excessive mid/upper treble. Splashy and a bit slow but with a very inviting midrange that doesn't compromise overall timbral accuracy in the pursuit of a bit of extra romance.

entries.name: Moondrop ILLUSTRIOUS
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.7/10, overall 5.98/10 (MSRP 900).
entries.quote: Warm, punchy, and more open than most passive IEMs. Slight low-treble flare and excess bloom, but balances listenability with texturing in the upper registers reasonably well.

entries.name: CrinEar Project Meta
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.58/10, overall 6.13/10 (MSRP 250).
entries.quote: Fantastic midrange, excessive bass and extremely excessive mid/upper treble. Good example of how otherwise excellent tuning can be ruined by the last two octaves. Great shell comfort for me.

entries.name: Symphonium Crimson
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.55/10, overall 5.61/10 (MSRP 1200).
entries.quote: Symphonium's most well-integrated bass + midrange tuning, marred by a 12 kHz spike of pure pain. Plenty of fun, but I am upset that it's so close to being excellent and flubs the treble so hard.

entries.name: Kiwi Ears Astral
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.53/10, overall 5.54/10 (MSRP 300).
entries.quote: Would be really rather solid if there wasn't a massive air spike causing any hi-hat cymbal to become pure white noise. Decent bass and really good midrange tuning.

entries.name: Sony IER-M9
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.53/10, overall 6.09/10 (MSRP 1000).
entries.quote: Solid midrange tuning, middling bass performance, slightly overly grainy/scratchy treble. Incredibly comfortable shell design, but docked one point for lack of venting.

entries.name: DUNU x Gizaudio Davinci
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.5/10, overall 5.11/10 (MSRP 300).
entries.quote: Excellent midrange + lower/mid treble, excessive bass and upper treble. V-shaped but not in a way that seems totally imbalanced. Nice sense of spaciousness.

entries.name: 64 Audio U4s
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.5/10, overall 5.87/10 (MSRP 1000).
entries.quote: Near identical to U12t but with a more present sub-bass and slightly less strident treble. Only tested with m20, may be better subjectively with a less bassy module.

entries.name: Symphonium Audio Helios
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.5/10, overall 4.83/10 (MSRP 1100).
entries.quote: An actually innovative take on a Harman-like signature; lean mids balanced by 3 kHz reduction + controlled low treble. One of the only *true* Sub-bass-onlybass boosts, which pairs with the contrast-tuned midrange for intense dynamism. Treble that shimmers in a good way provided you know what to expect and which tips may work for you. Insanely detailed, terrible ergonomics.

entries.name: grell TWS1X
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.48/10, overall 4.96/10 (MSRP 300).
entries.quote: Surprisingly normal sounding in the mids and bass (though quite warm), with a little bit of low treble flare in my ear (length mode?). Poor feature implementation/connectivity and shell design is also awkward in the ear.

entries.name: Audiosense AQ4
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.45/10, overall 5.56/10 (MSRP 150).
entries.quote: Overly bassy with very solid midrange timbre and slight lower treble flare causing graininess. Confused sounding, with driver flex; noticeable lack of venting.

entries.name: Kiwi Ears Quintet
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.45/10, overall 5.57/10 (MSRP 220).
entries.quote: Competent bass, surprisingly reasonable midrange tuning, with a slight bit of extra treble. A bit lean, but sensible.

entries.name: TruthEar Hola
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.4/10, overall 6.05/10 (MSRP 20).
entries.quote: Warm but not totally lacking nuance, a bit too flabby of bass and a bit too sharp of upper treble, but for the price... incredibly solid. RIP.

entries.name: 64 Audio U12t
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.4/10, overall 5.72/10 (MSRP 2000).
entries.quote: Quite similar to U6t but with less midrange coherence, marginally more annoying treble, and a slightly puffier bass presentation.

entries.name: Empire Ears Legend EVO
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.38/10, overall 4.86/10 (MSRP 3100).
entries.quote: Hilariously colored tuning that ultimately results in a super vivid/fun bass and midrange presentation that also happens to not have terrible treble. Weird shell fit/size.

entries.name: DUNU Glacier
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.35/10, overall 5.16/10 (MSRP 1350).
entries.quote: Kind of like Cadenza12 if, instead of natural midrange, it went full Harman. Incredibly robust, thick, and textured bass. Typical pitfalls of a Harman IEM re: thin mids and treble but I honestly really enjoy how vivid this one is. Shell is ridiculously big/heavy.

entries.name: ZIIGAAT ODYSSEY
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.3/10, overall 5.49/10 (MSRP 250).
entries.quote: Thinner and brighter than the original, lacks the comfy warm midrange that made the OG interesting while also having less density and dynamic wollop.

entries.name: TruthEar ZERO RED
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.25/10, overall 5.05/10 (MSRP 55).
entries.quote: IEF Neutral 2020's logical conclusion; a healthy bass shelf under 200 Hz to offset the honky mids, and a bit of extra low treble. Treble control is reliant on narrow bore tips. Balanced approach to a bass-focused presentation, but not neutral in overall timbre.

entries.name: TruthEar Gate
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.18/10, overall 5.85/10 (MSRP 20).
entries.quote: Harman but with less mid-bass, a little extra upper mid/low treble, but smoother mid/upper treble. My favorite Harman set due to getting its intensity from the midrange relationship instead of overly-boosted treble or bass.

entries.name: Moondrop x Crinacle: Dusk DSP Default
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.18/10, overall 4.87/10 (MSRP 330).
entries.quote: Good midrange timbre, excessive sub-bass and upper treble. Mediocre ergonomics, reliant on DSP for "intended" tuning, stock non-DSP tuning is thin, honky, and bright.

entries.name: Audiosense DT200
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.13/10, overall 6.14/10 (MSRP 150).
entries.quote: Soft, loose bass with overly-shimmery treble, but the midrange timbre is lovely. Incredibly small and well-molded shell, but unvented.

entries.name: ThieAudio Hype 4
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.13/10, overall 5.73/10 (MSRP 400).
entries.quote: Fun bass and slightly thin mids, with a ridiculous amount of upper treble. Colored as fuck, but occasionally fun.

entries.name: Shuoer EJ07M
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.13/10, overall 5.24/10 (MSRP 600).
entries.quote: A very reasonable take on IEF 2020; slightly clenched sounding midrange with just enough bass to offset the pointiness of vocals and guitars. Surprisingly listenable treble.

entries.name: Forte Ears Macbeth
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.08/10, overall 4.76/10 (MSRP 4000).
entries.quote: Loose-ish bass with a decent enough midrange, but with overdone treble. One of the ugliest IEMs I've ever seen.

entries.name: ThieAudio Valhalla
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 5.05/10, overall 4.86/10 (MSRP 2000).
entries.quote: Fun bass presentation with slightly forward, nasal midrange presentation and quite glassy, overbearing upper treble. Didn't really perceive much unique about it, not super dynamic, not super textured.

entries.name: Tangzu Zetian Wu Heyday
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.95/10, overall 5.42/10 (MSRP 200).
entries.quote: Probably the best planar IEM I've heard because it focuses quite a bit towards the upper mids instead of treble, which makes it sound quite textured and revealing despite the bass not having much palpability and the treble, typical of a planar, still being too shimmery and glisten-y.

entries.name: ThieAudio Hype 4 mk2
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.9/10, overall 5.25/10 (MSRP 400).
entries.quote: Softer bass than Mk1 but better mids, still with a ridiculous amount of upper treble that only kinda works when recordings don't have any air. Still colored as fuck, but meaningfully less fun than the original.

entries.name: TruthEar Hexa
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.88/10, overall 5.13/10 (MSRP 90).
entries.quote: Looks more neutral on a graph than it sounds to me; sub-bass dominant with thin midrange and sharp resonances at 8 & 11 kHz.

entries.name: Juzear Light Shuttle
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.88/10, overall 5.27/10 (MSRP 350).
entries.quote: Bloated sub/mid-bass, decent mids, glarey upper treble, basically an unremarkable Thieaudio IEM in different clothes.

entries.name: Sony IER-Z1R
