entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.85/10, overall 4.15/10 (MSRP 1700).
entries.quote: Novel and hyper-textured bass presentation due to wonky midrange + rough and glarey treble. One of the least ergonomic shell designs of all time.

entries.name: Symphonium Europa
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.83/10, overall 5.08/10 (MSRP 1200).
entries.quote: Only marginally better than Crimson in the treble while neutering what made Crimson fun and reasonably balanced (bass-to-midrange relationship).

entries.name: XENNS Tea PRO
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.8/10, overall 5.17/10 (MSRP 360).
entries.quote: Surprisingly thick sounding bass, but incoherent when moving up/down in pitch on bass instruments. Treble is ringy and splashy, midrange a little forward in a way that makes it sound pretty darn impactful.

entries.name: Symphonium Audio Triton
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.8/10, overall 4.08/10 (MSRP 900).
entries.quote: Reasonable-ish tonal profile, if a bit too lean, marred by extremely subpar comfort and a fairly unengaging bass profile.

entries.name: Nightjar  Duality
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.78/10, overall 4.81/10 (MSRP 3000).
entries.quote: Giga-bass but less coherent midrange integration than Singularity, leaner profile overall with harsher mid-treble.

entries.name: Unique Melody Multiverse Mentor
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.75/10, overall 4.58/10 (MSRP 4500).
entries.quote: Slightly too bloated, treble kind of lispy in that typical UM way, not noticeably technical. Kind of reminds me of Utopia 2022 in that it seems mid-focused but not all that textured?

entries.name: Moondrop LAN
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.68/10, overall 5.74/10 (MSRP 25).
entries.quote: Slightly bass lighter/brighter version of GATe's signature with slightly better ergonomics and leaner midrange. Ergo might be enough for people to prefer this one, but GATe's timbre is slightly better for me (likely due to treble)

entries.name: Campfire Andromeda 2020
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.68/10, overall 5.15/10 (MSRP 1100).
entries.quote: Warm but not overly bassy, a bit too bright and in a weird spot. Still probably the most spacious IEM I've heard due to its upper midrange/treble colorations. Very comfortable shell.

entries.name: Shuoer Cadenza 12
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.68/10, overall 4.44/10 (MSRP 2300).
entries.quote: Neutered what made the original interesting, now just a slightly too bright, way too expensive take on a neutral-ish W-shaped signature.

entries.name: 64 Audio Volür
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.63/10, overall 5.17/10 (MSRP 2000).
entries.quote: Like U4s but with more overbearing bass and nauseatingly sharp upper treble. Shame, the shell design is sick.

entries.name: Mysticraft Hex
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.58/10, overall 4.1/10 (MSRP 9000).
entries.quote: W-shaped signature typical of Lee but with slightly less puffy (but still puffy) bass and less annoying upper midrange and treble. Still too bloated, crunchy, and wispy. Get YU9 Que instead for less money.

entries.name: Sennheiser IE 900
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.53/10, overall 5.05/10 (MSRP 1700).
entries.quote: Dramatically W-shaped response with fun bass, interestingly textured midrange, and very over-boosted treble. Not neutral, but not trying to be. Comfort is good, though the included cable sucks.

entries.name: Moondrop KADENZ
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.48/10, overall 5.44/10 (MSRP 220).
entries.quote: Slightly boosted bass balanced very well with excess 2 kHz. Midrange timbre sucks but bass hits very hard. Oddly not much texture despite the midrange forwardness, Typical low-treble emphasis.

entries.name: YU9 Que
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.48/10, overall 4.61/10 (MSRP 400).
entries.quote: Bass very separated from everything else, fun for certain recordings but fluffy/overwhelming on most. Mids too crunchy due to 1.5 kHz forwardness but lacking textural intensity in the 3-5 kHz band; confused sounding. Low treble okay, upper treble annoyingly chirpy and sizzly. Mids/treble clearly compromised just to balance the bass shelf. At least people can buy this instead of Elysian.

entries.name: ThieAudio Monarch MKII
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.45/10, overall 3.92/10 (MSRP 1000).
entries.quote: Decent bass, but lean mids and a sandy, dry treble presentation. Stupidly designed shell with terrible comfort.

entries.name: Moondrop x Crinacle Blessing2 Dusk
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.35/10, overall 4.57/10 (MSRP 320).
entries.quote: Mildly incoherent bass to midrange integration with a slight buzziness around low treble, but with reasonable upper treble. Fit kind of annoying.

entries.name: Oriolus Trailli
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.33/10, overall 4.28/10 (MSRP 7000).
entries.quote: Mediocre midrange tuning, relaxed treble and a slightly overblown bass-shelf means its inoffensive but its also $7000

entries.name: TruthEar Nova
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.25/10, overall 4.94/10 (MSRP 150).
entries.quote: Harman basically to a T, but with a bit extra mid-treble to my ear. A bit grittier and sandier than other Harman IEMs, but also one of the better bass presentations.

entries.name: Kiwi Ears Septet
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.25/10, overall 4.74/10 (MSRP 230).
entries.quote: Potentially the limpest IEM I've heard. Absolutely erases all sense of note weight and dynamic punch. Extremely bright. Nice bass to midrange relationship but just overwhelmed completely by treble.

entries.name: I/O Sogno
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.25/10, overall 4.87/10 (MSRP 400).
entries.quote: Harman with marginally less mid-bass. GATe is a better version of this approach for me.

entries.name: Shuoer Galileo
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.23/10, overall 4.95/10 (MSRP 90).
entries.quote: Harman but with a treble resonance directly in my pain point. Sick shell design.

entries.name: Symphonium Titan
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.23/10, overall 4.67/10 (MSRP 1000).
entries.quote: Basshead meme with poorly integrated midrange and treble as well as a strangely blurred presentation despite the forwardness of treble.

entries.name: Ice Labs Prismatica
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.18/10, overall 4.29/10 (MSRP 900).
entries.quote: Warm with sloppy bass and treble, unremarkable aside from a decent midrange (that gets overshadowed near-completely)

entries.name: Letshuoer S08
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.13/10, overall 5.7/10 (MSRP 90).
entries.quote: Mediocre treble, though for a planar this is high praise. Midrange is very weird/center humped, but this does help the bass have moderate snappiness. Awesome comfort.

entries.name: AFUL Explorer
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 4.05/10, overall 5.47/10 (MSRP 120).
entries.quote: Boxy/confused midrange (IEF 2020) with a weird low treble valley and a bloaty bass shelf, not my jam but fine. Treble either sharp in the 10 kHz band (narrow bore) or a bit too wispy around 13 kHz (wide bore), medium bore rec'd. Exceptionally comfortable shell, decent value.

entries.name: ThieAudio Monarch MKIII
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.98/10, overall 3.91/10 (MSRP 1000).
entries.quote: More W-shaped than the predecessor; slightly better treble and more impactful bass at the cost of even worse midrange. Simialrly poor ergonomics, though maybe slightly improved.

entries.name: Kiwi Ears Étude
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.88/10, overall 4.42/10 (MSRP 100).
entries.quote: A bit too bumpy in the bass and quite forward in the early ear-gain. Treble surprisingly not super offensive but still has a slightly artificial hash to it (likely from what sounds like a mix of lower + upper treble elevations). Comfort is poor due to nozzle shape and microphonics.

entries.name: ZIIGAAT ZIIGAAT X JAY SERAPHIM
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.88/10, overall 4.81/10 (MSRP 250).
entries.quote: Overly boomy bass that is very disconnected from the thinned/hollow sounding midrange, paired with a shimmery, glassy treble response. Shell design is awesome, comfort is decent, sound profile just typical blobby bass + upper-treble boosted V-shape

entries.name: Moondrop Variations
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.83/10, overall 4.74/10 (MSRP 540).
entries.quote: Harman but with a little extra 1-2 kHz and more upper treble, neither of which is an improvement. Great shell comfort for me.

entries.name: Moondrop Ultrasonic
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.8/10, overall 4.1/10 (MSRP 80).
entries.quote: Slightly bloated bass, uneven midrange with slight honk, rough plasticky treble. Not exactly uncomfortable but definitely not comfy either.

entries.name: Apple AirPods Pro
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.8/10, overall 5.05/10 (MSRP 200).
entries.quote: Still great comfort, but weirdly midrange emphasized sound that sound simultaneously kind of basslet and kind of dark.

entries.name: DUNU Titan S2
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.75/10, overall 4.65/10 (MSRP 80).
entries.quote: Decent midrange for a single DD, but gritty treble and sloppy bass.

entries.name: Xenns Top Pro
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.73/10, overall 4.21/10 (MSRP 500).
entries.quote: Bloaty but still soft bass, decent mids, rough and slightly grainy lower/upper treble.

entries.name: BLON x HBB Z300
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.6/10, overall 4.34/10 (MSRP 45).
entries.quote: Clumsy take on a warm signature, too little 3 kHz and too much 1 kHz. Overly bassy. Kind of rough in the treble. Metal shell with poor molding.

entries.name: Kiwi Ears Orchestra Lite
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.6/10, overall 3.71/10 (MSRP 250).
entries.quote: Mediocre bass and midrange, competent treble control, terribly uncomfortable shell.

entries.name: Dunu Falcon Ultra
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.5/10, overall 4.37/10 (MSRP 220).
entries.quote: Surprisingly gritty and incoherent for a single DD, too much upper midrange and low treble.

entries.name: Sennheiser IE600
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.5/10, overall 4.18/10 (MSRP 900).
entries.quote: W-shaped response with quite forward bass, slight honk to the midrange, and very over-boosted treble. Comfort is good, though the included cable sucks.

entries.name: Samsung Galaxy Buds +
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.48/10, overall 3.83/10 (MSRP 100).
entries.quote: Harman, with all of the issues that comes with but in a very large and uncomfortable shell.

entries.name: Truthear Zero
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.45/10, overall 3.91/10 (MSRP 50).
entries.quote: Harman but with less sub-bass. The mid-bass is fun, the rest is pretty thin/harsh. Very poor comfort due to large nozzle.

entries.name: Etymotic ER4p
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.45/10, overall 4.06/10 (MSRP 350).
entries.quote: Very incisive due to essentially no bass or low midrange presence, magnifying glass into the upper midrange lends itself to great texturing. Virtually no sense of contrast, space, or naturalness.

entries.name: Ucotech RE-2
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.25/10, overall 4.38/10 (MSRP 90).
entries.quote: Basslet midrange focused set with terrible QC and kind of poor comfort, including a terrible stock cable. Super dynamic due to no bass and mid focus.

entries.name: KZ CRN
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.23/10, overall 4.17/10 (MSRP 35).
entries.quote: Competent midrange + bass integration but the length mode around 7 kHz is among the worst I've heard. It is so bad it gaslit myriad reviewers into saying the IEM had BA timbre when the BAs were not even playing.

entries.name: ZIIGAAT ARCANIS
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.18/10, overall 3.92/10 (MSRP 300).
entries.quote: IEF 2020 mids done wrong. Has all of the honk and fatigue but none of the texturing or crackle. Bass is surprisingly slow given this midrange tuning, treble is rough and grainy.

entries.name: ZiiGaat Estrella
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.18/10, overall 3.78/10 (MSRP 400).
entries.quote: Giga-incoherent. W shape but where the bass feels absolutely disjointed from everything else. Brightness in the mid/upper treble that makes vocals sound overly-sharpened and cymbais sound like they have rivets drilled into them. Surprisingly weird imaging.

entries.name: Creative Aurvana Ace 2
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.15/10, overall 3.42/10 (MSRP 80).
entries.quote: Definition of V-shaped; harsh papery low treble and tons of excess bass. Uncomfortable shell design.

entries.name: Moondrop Blessing 3
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.13/10, overall 3.87/10 (MSRP 300).
entries.quote: Thin, slightly shouty, basically no bass presence, reasonably textured treble. This one's purely for the weebs.

entries.name: SHOZY P20
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 3.08/10, overall 3.94/10 (MSRP 140).
entries.quote: Bloated bass, typical 14.2mm planar mids (slightly shouty, slightly slow) and too much upper treble. Better sound can be had cheaper.

entries.name: Elysian Annihilator (2023)
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.95/10, overall 2.79/10 (MSRP 3500).
entries.quote: Loose fluffy bass, honky incoherent mids, ridiculously bright treble. Shell comfort typical of flagship driver spam, meaning extremely large & uncomfortable.

entries.name: Kiwi Ears Quartet
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.9/10, overall 3.91/10 (MSRP 110).
entries.quote: Absolute mudfest, only for the warmest of warmpoo enjoyers.

entries.name: 7th Acoustics Supernova
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.9/10, overall 3.18/10 (MSRP 850).
entries.quote: Grainy, limp, thin, small, basically everything I don't like about all-BA IEMs but with a pretty punishing low/mid treble tuning.

entries.name: Kiwi Ears Orchestra 2
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.88/10, overall 3.45/10 (MSRP 350).
entries.quote: Extremely bright in the upper treble, impossible to ignore sizzle. Mids are thin and slightly shouty in the 1-2 kHz region, mid-bass is forward enough to slightly balance it out wide-band but on guitars or piano the coloration is noticeable enough to ruin it.

entries.name: Punch Audio Martilo
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.8/10, overall 3.59/10 (MSRP 320).
entries.quote: Some of the most overboosted, bloaty, boomy bass I've heard. Kick drums have no attack, bass guitars have one note that'll be boosted crazily and the next note will be weirdly recessed causing literal melodic intelligibility issues. Mids are solid, treble is splashy and tizzy.

entries.name: Shure SE215
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.68/10, overall 4.74/10 (MSRP 100).
entries.quote: Grainy as hell, slightly bloated, a bit shouty, but so goddamn comfortable. Easy skip in current year when there's so much good stuff under $100, but none of the new stuff is nearly this comfortable.

entries.name: CCA CRA
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.65/10, overall 3.89/10 (MSRP 25).
entries.quote: Apparently has a solid bass presentation, couldn't hear it over the disgustingly bright treble.

entries.name: Shuoer DZ4
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.58/10, overall 3.24/10 (MSRP 80).
entries.quote: Like a slightly less shouty ER2XR with better comfort/venting.

entries.name: Etymotic ER2XR
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.33/10, overall 3.33/10 (MSRP 105).
entries.quote: Slightly better bass than the ER4 but much worse treble, otherwise similarly "Oops! All Upper Midrange" tuning.

entries.name: Sennheiser IE 200
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.33/10, overall 3.76/10 (MSRP 160).
entries.quote: W-shaped response with lacking bass, unnatural midrange, and very over-boosted treble. Comfort is good, though the included cable sucks.

entries.name: Symphonium Giant
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.2/10, overall 3.42/10 (MSRP 600).
entries.quote: Bloated, slow bass. Unnatural, incoherent midrange. Ringy, plasticky treble. No idea who this is for or why it exists.

entries.name: 7Hz Salnotes Dioko
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.13/10, overall 2.94/10 (MSRP 100).
entries.quote: Treble so sharp it instilled a fear of planar IEMs that persists to this day.

entries.name: ooopusX Op.24
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 2.03/10, overall 2.75/10 (MSRP 45).
entries.quote: Shockingly rough, crashy sounding treble with a tone knob that doesn't work and a worse, shoutier take on a Harman bass/midrange tuning.

entries.name: 7Hz Salnotes Zero
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 1.98/10, overall 2.96/10 (MSRP 20).
entries.quote: Thin and small sounding, harsh treble. Bad comfort.

entries.name: Shure KSE1500
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 1.85/10, overall 3.73/10 (MSRP 3000).
entries.quote: One of the worst sounding IEMs I've ever listened to. People will swear up and down that it's got "tech," but its just treble murder.

entries.name: Campfire Andromeda Emerald Sea
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 1.7/10, overall 2.9/10 (MSRP 1400).
entries.quote: One of the most oppressively bassy IEMs I've ever heard. Easy avoid unless you want to stick your head in a vat full of mud.

entries.name: Etymotic ER2SE
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 1.63/10, overall 2.73/10 (MSRP 105).
entries.quote: Much worse treble than ER4, otherwise similarly "Oops! All Upper Midrange" tuning.

entries.name: Truthear Zero Blue2
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 1.43/10, overall 2.77/10 (MSRP 55).
entries.quote: Harman but somehow worse in all aspects; thinner mids, looser bass, and some of the worst treble I've ever heard.

entries.name: Audeze LCD-i3
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 1.1/10, overall 1.45/10 (MSRP 900).
entries.quote: Weird in so many ways. Don't waste your time with any of the LCD-i series unless you specifically want the weirdest IEMs of all time.

entries.name: Delta/United Airline Buds
entries.verdict: Listener rates sound 0/10, overall 0.25/10 (MSRP 0).
entries.quote: Literally non-functional for intelligible playback
